verdict.rationale: Warp documents that cloud agents can run on "your own" infrastructure via self-hosted workers. Its client source code is released under AGPL v3, so users can audit it and run it themselves. However, nothing shows the backend services the core product depends on (accounts, AI routing, Warp Drive, the Oz orchestration control plane) can be self-hosted. Missing for 10: self-hostable backend/control plane, a self-hosting deployment guide, independent or hands-on corroboration of a self-hosted setup.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Cloud agents are autonomous, background agents that run on Warp’s cloud infrastructure or your own
API keys let the Oz CLI, cloud agents, and self-hosted workers authenticate without human interaction.
Read and audit Warp’s client source code at warpdotdev/warp, open source under AGPL v3
Warp’s source code is now available at github.com/warpdotdev/warp with an AGPL license.
